questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution pertains to the Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution: Article 51-A in Part IV-A of the Constitution contains the Fundamental Duties. These were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976. Originally, there were 10 duties, but an 11th (relating to education) was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the right of the Governor to address and to send messages to the House (or Houses) of the state legislature?
questions.solution: Article 175 deals with the right of the Governor to address and send messages to the House or Houses of the State Legislature. This ensures communication between the executive head of the state and the legislative body regarding pending bills or other matters.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution are mentioned in which Article?
questions.solution: Article 51 A is the specific article that lists the Fundamental Duties. It was incorporated following the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee to remind citizens that rights and duties are correlative.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all the courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution: Article 141 states that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. This establishes the principle of stare decisis and ensures uniformity in the judicial system across the country.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution: Article 97 mentions the salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha. These are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.question: From which of the following Constitutions is the idea of ‘Charter of Fundamental Rights’ adopted in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The idea of a 'Charter of Fundamental Rights' (Bill of Rights) was adopted from the Constitution of the United States of America. It forms the bedrock of individual liberties in India, protecting citizens against arbitrary state action.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution is commonly referred to as the ‘Magna Carta of India’?
questions.solution: Part III of the Indian Constitution is commonly referred to as the ‘Magna Carta of India’. It contains a comprehensive list of justiciable fundamental rights that are essential for the material and moral development of citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a basic feature of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The statement 'Drawn from one source' is NOT a basic feature. The Indian Constitution is known for being a 'patchwork' drawn from various world constitutions (UK, US, Ireland, Canada, etc.). It is the lengthiest written constitution and a blend of rigidity and flexibility.

questions.question: According to Dr. BR Ambedkar’s views, which of the following is the key feature of the Directive Principles of the Constitution?
questions.solution: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Directive Principles of State Policy as a 'Novel Feature' of the Indian Constitution. He emphasized that though they are non-justiciable, they are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.question: The 42nd Amendment of the Indian Constitution (1976) states that India is a/an __________________ nation.
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the word 'Secular' to the Preamble. This officially declared India to be a nation that protects all religions equally and does not have a state religion. The words 'Socialist' and 'Integrity' were also added at this time.

questions.question: The minimum strength of the Council of Ministers in a state as per the Indian Constitution is ________ .
questions.solution: The minimum strength of the Council of Ministers in a state is fixed at 12 persons (including the Chief Minister). Note: The maximum strength cannot exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that state.

questions.question: Who has the power to make law and policies for the country, as per the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Parliament has the supreme power to make laws and policies for the country. It consists of the President and the two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Political parties and pressure groups may influence policy, but the legal authority rests with the legislature.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct in the context of the Indian Constitution?

1.There are three major organs of the government, namely Legislature, Executive and Judiciary.

2.A separation of functions rather than powers is followed.

3.All organs of the government are independent.
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. There are three organs: Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary. India follows a separation of functions with a system of checks and balances. Correction: Statement 3 is technically incorrect because the organs are interdependent (e.g., the Executive is responsible to the Legislature).

questions.question: How many fundamental duties were added by the 42nd Constitution Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.solution: Exactly 10 fundamental duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. The 11th duty was added much later in 2002.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the special powers of the Governors according to the Indian Constitution?

A.The Governor of Nagaland shall have special responsibility related to law and order in the State.

B.The Governor of Manipur will submit a special annual report to the President on the administration of hilly areas in the State.

C.The Governor of Sikkim shall have special responsibility for peace and for an equitable arrangement for ensuring the social and economic advancement of different sections.

D.The Governor of Arunachal Pradesh shall have special responsibility with respect to law and order in the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
questions.solution: All statements (A, B, C, and D) are correct. The Constitution provides special responsibilities to Governors of certain states (Nagaland, Manipur, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh) to address specific regional requirements, law and order, or tribal interests under Articles 371-371H.

questions.question: Who is the Chief Executive Head of the State?
questions.solution: The Governor is the Chief Executive Head of the State. Like the President at the Centre, the Governor is a nominal head, while the real executive authority is exercised by the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.

questions.question: Among the following, which is not a qualification for membership in the Vidhan Sabha
questions.option_1: Have attained the age of 25 Years
questions.option_2: Not hold any office of profit
questions.solution: 'Knowledge of Politics' is NOT a formal qualification for membership in the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly). Constitutional requirements include being a citizen of India, being at least 25 years old, and not holding an office of profit.

questions.question: In which year were four new Directive Principles added to the original list?
questions.solution: In 1976 (via the 42nd Amendment), four new Directive Principles were added: Article 39 (opportunities for healthy development of children), Article 39A (equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (participation of workers in management), and Article 48A (protection of environment).

questions.question: Generally, Directive Principles are ________.
questions.solution: Directive Principles are generally positive directions or instructions to the State to work toward the welfare of the people. Unlike Fundamental Rights, which are often negative (prohibitive) in nature by restricting state power, DPSPs tell the state what to do.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty of an Indian citizen?
questions.option_2: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.option_3: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
questions.option_4: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
questions.solution: 'To vote in public elections' is NOT a fundamental duty listed in the Constitution. While it is a crucial civic duty and a legal right, it is not included in the list under Article 51A. The other options are explicitly mentioned duties.

questions.question: Under the provisions of Article 22 of the Constitution, the Advisory Board shall consist of persons who are appointed or eligible to be appointed as __________.
questions.solution: Under Article 22, an Advisory Board (for preventive detention) must consist of persons who are, or have been, or are qualified to be appointed as Judges of a High Court. This acts as a safeguard against arbitrary detention beyond three months.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding State Legislatures?

A. Notwithstanding anything contained in Part XVII, but subject to the provisions of Article 348, the business in the Legislature of a State shall be transacted in the official language(s) of the State or in Hindi or English

B. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or the Chairman of the Legislative Council may permit any member to speak in his mother tongue.

C. Only the Supreme Court has the power to inquire into the proceedings of the State Legislature.
questions.solution: Statements A and B are correct. Business is transacted in official state languages, Hindi, or English. The Speaker/Chairman can allow a member to speak in their mother tongue. Correction: Statement C is false; Article 212 prevents courts from inquiring into the internal proceedings of the Legislature.

questions.question: If a person who is arrested, is NOT produced before the Magistrate within 24 hours from the time of arrest, he will be entitled to be released on the writ of ________.
questions.solution: The writ of Habeas Corpus (meaning 'to have the body') is applicable here. If a person is detained without being produced before a magistrate within 24 hours, this writ can be used to secure their release from illegal custody.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India consists of ________ judges and Chief Judges of India.
questions.solution: The Supreme Court currently consists of 33 judges and one Chief Justice of India (total strength of 34). This strength was increased from 31 to 34 by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.

questions.question: In which of the following schedules of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 is the most common wild cat in India 'Felis chaus' listed?
questions.solution: The Jungle Cat (Felis chaus), which is common in India, is listed under Schedule II of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. This provides it with a high degree of protection, and trade/hunting is strictly regulated.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding conditions required to recognise as a political party in India?

A.If a political party is treated as a recognised political party in four or more States, it shall be known as a ‘National Party’ throughout the whole of India.

B.If a political party is treated as a recognised political party in less than four States, it shall be known as a ‘State Party’ in the State or States in which it is so recognised.

C.National Parties need only one proposer for filing the nomination and are also entitled for two sets of electoral rolls free of cost.
questions.solution: All statements (A, B, and C) are correct. A National Party must be recognized in 4+ states. National parties get benefits like a single proposer for nominations and free electoral rolls. A party recognized in fewer than 4 states remains a State Party.

questions.question: How many members (elected and nominated) were there in the Council of State under the Government of India Act 1919 passed by the Parliament of the United Kingdom to expand participation of Indians in the government of India?
questions.solution: Under the Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms), the Council of State (Upper House) consisted of 60 members. Of these, 33 were elected and 27 were nominated by the Governor-General. This was the first time bicameralism was introduced at the central level.
